title: Supplier switch cost simulator and enterprise onboarding playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a decision support artifact (interactive simulator + written playbook) that helps Customer Success, Sales Engineering, and GTM evaluate the true cost and risk of switching model suppliers across regulated verticals (finance, healthcare, gov). The simulator will model latency, per-token cost, SLA risk, onboarding friction, embeddings drift, and contractual budgeting over a 12-month horizon. The playbook will include an onboarding checklist, preflight tests, and negotiated contract language suggestions for providers and capacity tiers.

Scope:
- Inputs: model price curves (hosted/dedicated), expected QPS and token profiles, embedding refresh cadence, quantization/compatibility flags, compliance constraints (data residency, KMS), and trial-to-production conversion rates.
- Outputs: NPV of switch costs, break-even analysis vs fallback, recommended staging rollout (canary size, fallbacks), key negotiation levers, and a prioritized onboarding checklist.
- Artefacts: web-based simulator (spreadsheet-first prototype + lightweight React UI), PDF playbook, customizable slides for AE/SE teams, preflight test harness (test prompts + evaluation rubric).

Success metrics:
- Simulator used in >10 enterprise deals during Q4 trials.
- Reduction in average legal/ops negotiation time for model onboarding from 18 days to <10 days for target accounts.
- 95% of Post-Onboard incidents attributed to model mismatch are anticipated by the simulator's risk flags.

Stakeholders:
- Product Management (owner): Aisha Patel
- Engineering: Marcus Chen (assignee), ENG runtime leads for cost curves
- Sales Engineering: Priya Srinivasan
- Legal & Security: Ana Rodrigues (contract templates)
- Customer Success: Tom Alvarez (pilot program)

Key trade-offs and decisions to make:
- Fidelity vs speed: build high-fidelity kernel that requires runtime telemetry (slower) vs spreadsheet prototype for immediate GTM impact. Decision: prototype spreadsheet first, iterate to a lightweight UI if adoption > threshold.
- Scope of provider coverage: focus first on top-5 providers and Redwood Dedicated variants to limit engineering inputs.
- Onboarding test depth: include an embedding drift simulator (adds complexity) but valuable for search use cases — include as optional advanced module.

Risks:
- Getting accurate price curves and contractual data from providers; mitigation: use public pricing + anonymized deal extracts + engineering measured perf.
- Legal sensitivities around recommended contract language; mitigation: include legal sign-off on playbook snippets and present as suggestions not legal advice.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1-2: requirements, capture inputs from SE and legal, spreadsheet prototype (v0).
- Week 3-4: pilot simulator with 3 active deals, iterate.
- Week 5-7: polish playbook, create slides and checklist, run enablement with AE/SE.
- Week 8: ship v1 and measure usage.

Open questions:
- Which pricing components should be modeled as fixed vs variable (setup fees, reservation discounts)? Need input from finance.
- Will customers accept suggested contract language or require bespoke legal review? Plan to A/B in pilot accounts.
